Class 3 · Chapter 9 of 10

Number, letter and picture patterns

Complete number series, letter patterns and picture rules.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Picture charts, bars and tables. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can complete a number series.
  • I can complete a letter pattern.
  • I can copy a picture rule.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 5

Find the number rule

Look at how far it is from one number to the next.

4, 10, 16, 22: each number is 6 more, so the rule is add 6. The next number is 28.

Screen 2 of 5

Doubling patterns

1, 2, 4, 8: each number is double the one before.

The jumps get bigger each time. The next number is 16.

Screen 3 of 5

Letter patterns

The alphabet goes A, B, C, D, E, F, G. A C E G skips one letter each time.

The next letter after G is I.

Screen 4 of 5

Turning pictures

A picture can turn a quarter turn each time.

Up, right, down, then left. After left it goes back to up.

Screen 5 of 5

Use the same rule again

If a rule turns a picture, use the same rule on the next picture.

Up goes to right, so right goes to down.

Words to know
rule
What changes by the same amount or in the same way each time.
term
One number or picture in a pattern.
sequence
A list of numbers or pictures that follows a rule.

For parents

What your child learns

Patterns are about finding the rule. Your child continues number series, steps through the alphabet and applies a picture rule to a new picture.

A common slip

Children often check only the first jump. Ask them to test the rule on every pair of neighbours. For letters, count the skipped letters, not the letters you land on.

5-minute home activity: Rule detectives

  1. Say 4, 10, 16, 22 and ask what comes next.
  2. Ask what the rule is: add 6.
  3. Now try letters: A, C, E, G. Ask what comes next and why.
